survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note does not analyze student-level ILSA microdata (no assessment administration, sampling frame, or respondent-level dataset is used). As a result, there are no plausible values, no item responses, and no survey-weight variables to apply for estimation. The document describes governance structures and allocation of responsibilities/expenditure across subnational government levels (central, regional, county, municipal) rather than estimating statistical relationships from a complex survey. If analysts were to extend this note with ILSA microdata, they would need to use the official ILSA sampling weights and replicate weights provided with the microdata for variance estimation, but such weighting is not part of the present document.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a policy/governance country note and does not perform empirical statistical modeling on ILSA cognitive achievement outcomes. Because there is no PV-based dependent variable (and no student-level assessment dataset), plausible values handling is not applicable. Similarly, missing-data handling is not reported because no microdata cleaning/imputation procedure is conducted in the note.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No ILSA/NAEP/PIRLS/TIMSS/PISA microdata sample is used. The note is descriptive and covers governance arrangements in Poland; therefore, no analytic subsample is defined.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Poland country note provides a descriptive overview of how adult skills systems are governed across subnational levels (central, regional, county, municipal) and how responsibilities and funding/expenditure are allocated. It is part of a broader OECD review covering 38 OECD countries, with the Poland note published in June 2025 after review by Polish government representatives. The note uses governance tables (e.g., allocation of responsibilities across policy areas such as VET, HVET, CET, AE, and ALMP) and an infographic to map stakeholders and their roles, rather than analyzing student assessment data. No ILSA assessment cycle, grade, domain, plausible values, or statistical performance metrics are reported because the document is not an empirical large-scale assessment study. Consequently, there are no ML models, predictive targets, or benchmarks to interpret for education outcomes.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a non-empirical policy/governance document without an original ILSA-style microdata analysis. Therefore, fields related to ML modeling, plausible values, missing-data handling, and student sampling/weights are structurally absent by design. The extraction is limited to governance descriptions and responsibility allocation tables, which do not support the schema’s empirical ML outcome fields.
